steps.text: Welcome, {player_name}.
The night before the end was unnaturally quiet.
This was it. Our last moment of peace.
Getting ready?
Always. You should be meditating, not making small talk.
I just... wanted to say thank you, Eve. For everything.
Gratitude is a liability on the battlefield. Don't thank me. Just survive.
That's not enough anymore. I don't want to just survive. I want to live. I want to see that tavern you're always talking about. The one by the sea.
Don't talk about 'after.' There is no 'after.' There is only the next fight.
Why are you so afraid to hope?
Because hope gets people killed! Hope is what makes you drop your guard for one second. And one second is all it takes.
The last time I made plans for 'after'... I lost my best friend.
Her voice was sharp, but underneath it, I heard it. A deep, ancient pain. The ghost she carried with her every single day.
But we were happy sometimes, weren't we? It wasn't all just fighting and survival.
Happiness is a fleeting luxury.
Like that day in the market? When I tried the Dragon's Breath skewers?
(V.O. - Clear, amused) You are, without a doubt, the biggest idiot I've ever met. What did you think 'Dragon's Breath' meant?
(V.O. - Choking) I thought it was just a cool name! Is my tongue supposed to be on fire?!
(V.O. - A small snort, then a full, beautiful laugh) Just drink some milk. And try not to die. It would be a waste of my training.
That laugh. It was rare, and it was real. I'd fight a thousand wars to hear it again.
...You were choking. It was a tactical assessment. You're a liability when you can't breathe.
Right. 'Tactical'.
I'm going to get us there, Eve. To that tavern. We're going to sit on the coast and watch the sunset, and you're going to tell me stories about Anne. The real stories. The good ones.
You... you don't know what you're saying.
I know I'm making a promise. And I intend to keep it.
And in that moment, I remembered. The rain... the smell of wet earth after a desperate battle. The impossible feeling of victory.
Her hands, cold against my face. The quiet admission that she had allowed herself to hope again, because of me.
A future we had earned. A future that was stolen from us. A future I would reclaim.
Why do you look like that? Like you've just seen a ghost.
Just... making up my mind.
Fine.
She pressed her lucky silver coin into my hand. It felt heavy. Like a pact.
It's a loan. You give it back when you buy me that drink. Don't you dare lose it.
I won't. I promise.
A promise made in the dark.
A promise I would tear reality apart to keep.
Lyrel? Are you okay?
Oh! {mc_name}! Of course! Just thinking about tomorrow! We're going to win, and then we can finally get back to the forest. I'm excited!
She was building a fortress of cheerfulness, and the walls were paper-thin.
You sound like you're trying to convince yourself.
It's okay to be afraid, Lyrel. The forest is quiet now, but we both know it's still hurting.
My own people said it was a cursed grave. That I was a fool for trying to tend to a corpse...
It wasn't a corpse. It was a wound. And you were the only one brave enough to stay and listen to it scream.
I'll never forget the first time you showed me the 'cancer'.
She hadn't just shown me a blighted grove. She had shown me a mass grave, a monument to the horrors of war.
The faces of soldiers, fused into bark and soil, their silent screams a constant hum of pain under our feet.
And in her tears, I saw her true purpose. Not just to heal trees, but to give peace to a thousand forgotten souls.
They called you a traitor because they chose to run from that pain. You were the only one loyal enough to face it.
(A choked sob) I just... I didn't want them to be alone.
And you weren't alone either. Not after that day.
And I remembered the day our shared purpose bore fruit. The day he chose empathy over violence.
The forest's rage had taken her, twisting her pain into a weapon aimed at the world. It screamed for vengeance.
And he had walked into the storm, defenseless, and offered it comfort instead.
That embrace... it didn't just save her. It saved the forest's soul.
We did it once, Lyrel. We faced its rage and showed it another way. We can do it again.
That day... you saved more than just me.
She placed the warm, faintly glowing Heartwood seed in my palm.
The forest is quiet now, but the war will make it scream again. Promise me, Cyan. That you'll remember the lesson we learned.
That you'll choose to heal, not to harm. That you'll be the heart, even when the world demands a sword.
The world has enough swords. I promise, Lyrel. We will be its heart. Together.
A promise made in the dark.
A promise that would be shattered by a world that had no room for a heart.
The world ended with the sound of thunder.
The battle was a nightmare. Anne was a ghost, a whirlwind of silver I could barely track.
Eve was the rock in the storm, her daggers a desperate shield against the hurricane.
And then, I saw it. A moment Eve had paid for in blood.
An opening. A clear, unguarded path straight through the enemy lines. Straight towards Eclia.
The 'Good End'. The path to victory she was creating for me.
(VOICE, shouting over the din) The path is clear! Go, Cyan! That's an order! WIN THE DAMN WAR!
What about you?!
My life is less important than the mission! I'll hold her here! GO!
I looked at the path to victory. Then I looked at her.
And I remembered the promise I made by the campfire.
A promise not about war, but about a tavern by the sea.
My promise was to YOU! I'm not leaving you!
(VOICE, filled with fury and desperation) You damn fool!
And in that moment, I turned my back on the world.
I chose the 'Bad End'. I chose her.
My defiance, my choice... it cost her everything.
Distracted by my refusal, her guard dropped for a fraction of a second.
It was all the time Anne needed.
A terrible, silent tableau under the Blood Moon's gaze. Impaled on the hero's greatsword, her own daggers buried in her ghost, she had won the battle and lost everything.
The world went silent. I don't remember running. I remember crawling.
(VOICE, a choked scream) EVE!
I reached her side. Her blood was hot on my hands.
(A weak, raspy cough) Heh... Took you long enough... rookie.
Don't talk! I can... my runes... I can fix this!
(A faint, tired smile) Save your mana... It's too late for... ghosts...
Finally... put her to rest. My last... loose end.
Don't say that! Don't... what about our promise? The tavern by the sea... you promised you'd teach me how to cheat at cards!
(Her eyes soften. For a moment, the hardened assassin is gone.)
The first rule... kid... is never play a game... you can't win...
My magic sputtered, useless against a wound that had already claimed her soul. And in that moment of absolute despair, my mind broke free.
(V.O. - Clear, amused) You are, without a doubt, the biggest idiot I've ever met. What did you think 'Dragon's Breath' meant?
(V.O. - Choking) I thought it was just a cool name!
A memory of a time when the only pain was the spice on my tongue. A time when her laugh felt like it could last forever.
Her lucky coin, the one she'd loaned me, slipped from her belt.
I caught it before it hit the mud. It was already cold.
Cyan... The path... Lyrel...
Go... Don't let my win... be for nothing...
(Sobbing) No... Eve, please...
Her head lolled to the side. Her eyes, which had seen too much war, finally saw nothing at all.
I had stayed. I had kept my promise to not leave her.
And in doing so, I had lost her forever.
And in the sudden, deafening silence, I heard it.
A final, catastrophic shatter of green energy from across the battlefield.
The life force of a forest... and a friend... being extinguished.
I had chosen. And the price was everything.
The world ended with the sound of thunder.
But my focus wasn't on the clashing of swords. It was on the screaming of the earth.
Lyrel was at the heart of it, a conduit for the forest's rage. Green, thorny vines erupted around her, holding back the tide of monsters, but they were crawling up her arms, corrupting her.
(VOICE, shouting) The path is clear! Cyan, now! It's the only way!
I saw it. A clean path to victory, bought with blood. The soldier's path. The hero's path.
But my promise to Lyrel wasn't about being a hero.
(Shouting back) I can't leave her! She's losing control!
There's no time! She's a lost cause! We have to-
NO! The promise was to be the heart! Not another sword!
I turned my back on Eve. I turned my back on victory.
I chose the 'Bad End'. I chose our impossible promise.
I ran towards her, not with a weapon drawn, but with my hands outstretched.
The corrupted vines lashed out, but I pushed through, my runes flaring as a desperate, flickering shield.
(VOICE, a distorted chorus of rage and pain) STAY BACK! YOU WILL NOT HARM THIS SACRED GROUND!
I'm not here to harm it, Lyrel! I'm here to help you hold it! Let me share the burden!
I reached her, and just like I did once before, I wrapped my arms around her, trying to be the anchor in her storm.
For a moment, I felt the rage quiet. I felt her presence, small and terrified, inside the hurricane of power.
And in that moment, my mind clung to the memory of the last time this had happened.
I remembered the forest's heart, when my embrace had been enough. When my empathy had broken the curse and brought her back from the brink.
A memory of a time when a simple act of trust was enough to save the world.
But this wasn't a cursed grove. This was a war. And trust was not enough.
A wave of pure hatred from the battlefield slammed into her barrier, and I felt the tether snap. The storm inside her broke free.
The light pouring from her was blinding. The power was too much. It was going to explode, taking the entire battlefield with it.
But then I felt her hand, weak but firm, on my chest.
(VOICE, no longer a chorus, but her own, breathless and serene) ...It's okay, Cyan...
(Sobbing) Lyrel, no! Hold on! Just hold on!
Don't... make that face... It doesn't suit a hero...
Look...
She tilted her head towards the ground where the monstrous flowers were blooming, feeding on her life force, purifying the blighted soil.
I'm healing it... I'm giving them peace... just like we promised...
This isn't healing! This is suicide!
(A weak, beautiful, heartbreaking smile) Isn't it... beautiful...? What we made... together...?
And then she pushed me away with the last of her strength.
Live...

A silent nova of pure life energy erupted from her. It didn't destroy. It *healed*. The monsters caught in the blast dissolved into motes of light. The corrupted earth bloomed. The very air felt clean.
And at the center of that impossible garden, there was nothing left of her at all.
She had kept her promise. In her final moments, she had chosen to heal.
My own hand, shaking, went to the pouch at my belt.
The Heartwood seed, her last piece of home, crumbled to dust. Her promise was fulfilled. Mine was broken forever.
And in the quiet hum of the new life she had created, I heard it.
The unmistakable sound of a body hitting the ground. A single, final sword strike.
Silence.
I had chosen to be the heart. And in a world of swords, the heart is always the first thing to be broken.
The mood in Ironhold was suffocating. Soldiers ran drills in the courtyard. The air smelled of smoke and sharpened steel.
The intelligence you gathered in the Silent Forest was accurate. The South has been using the 'Underground Road' beneath the Dragon's Tooth mountains for months.
But the situation has escalated. Our sensors indicate a massive buildup of magical signatures moving toward the surface.
A buildup? Like an army?
An invasion force. They are attempting to establish a beachhead on our side of the mountains. If they open that door, Ironhold will be overrun within the hour.
And you wish for us to engage them?
No. I want you to close the door. Permanently.
This is Captain Vance of the 4th Engineering Corps. He and his team are carrying rune-charges designed to collapse the tunnel entrance.
Your mission is simple: Escort Vance to the site, protect the Engineers while they plant the charges, and extract. Do not engage the enemy unless compromised.
We seal the tunnel, we stop the invasion. No fighting required.
Precisely. It is a defensive measure to secure our homes. A non-lethal solution to a lethal problem.
Hey, 'Captain'. That's a lot of crates for a simple tunnel seal. What exactly are you packing in there?
Geological destabilizers. The rock here is reinforced with old granite. We need to be sure.
Standard charges would crack the granite. Those crates are lead-lined. That's usually for unstable mana-cores. You trying to seal the tunnel or blow the mountain off the map?
The Southern forces are likely using Earth magic to reinforce the tunnel from the inside. We need overwhelming force to break their hold.
Brandt is correct about the geology, but... the resonance coming from those crates is immense. It feels... volatile. Aggressive.
War is volatile, Elf. Do you want the tunnel closed or not?
Eve, Lyrel, it's fine. We're just collapsing a cave to keep them out. If we don't do this, people die.
We'll take the job, Brandt.
Good. Speed is of the essence. Vance has the coordinates. Move out immediately.
I don't like this. Vance isn't an engineer. He moves like a sapper. A demolitionist.
Agreed. That payload is excessive. If triggered incorrectly, the seismic shockwave could travel miles.
Keep your eyes on the 'Engineers', not just the South. I have a bad feeling we're the ones holding the match.
Come on, guys! Let's seal this up and go home!
Cyan marched forward, believing he was a shield for the North.
He didn't realize he was escorting the hammer that would break the peace.
The climb was grueling. The air grew thin and cold as they ascended the Dragon's Tooth. Captain Vance set a punishing pace, his 'Engineers' moving with silent, athletic endurance.
Look at them. They aren't carrying those crates like cargo. They're carrying them like tactical gear. And I saw the one on the left check his crossbow three times in the last hour.
Engineers build bridges, Lyrel. These guys look like they burn them.
I share your concern. I have been analyzing the magical signature of the crates. It is... dense. Earth magic mixed with unstable Fire salts.
It is not designed to seal a tunnel. It is designed to shatter a tectonic plate.
They reached the coordinates. A dark cave mouth gaped in the mountainside—the tunnel exit.
Secure the perimeter. My men will prime the charges.
The clouds parted, revealing the world below the peaks. It wasn't the grey stone and pine of the North. It was lush, green, and vibrant.
A town nestled in the valley, its red-tiled roofs glowing in the sun.
That town...
A jolt of recognition hit Cyan like a physical blow. The terraced gardens. The central plaza with the sun-dial mosaic. The way the river was diverted through the streets.
I know those streets. I used to run through a market like that. I used to buy spice-bread from a baker near a fountain just like that one.
It's... familiar. It looks like... home.
By the Elders...
Cyan, look at the angle of the slope. The geography here acts as a funnel.
If we detonate those charges here, the rockslide won't just block the cave. It will cascade.
Cascade?
Millions of tons of rock... falling directly onto that valley. It will erase that town.
What? But... Vance said it was a defensive seal!
He lied. It's not a seal. It's an execution.
Captain! Stop! You can't set those off here!
That valley is a supply hub for the enemy. It is a valid military target.
It's a town! I know that architecture! Those are homes! There are families down there!
They are Southerners. They are the enemy. Stand down, adventurer. You are paid to guard, not to think.
No! I won't let you bury them!
Whoa! Easy!
The standoff was instant. The 'Defensive Mission' had shattered in seconds.
This mission is sanctioned by High Command. Interfere, and you will be executed for treason.
I don't care! I remember... I remember what it's like down there! They aren't monsters!
He's right, Captain. They aren't monsters.
But you are about to see what happens when you threaten their cubs.
Fenrir?!
You... you're alive! And you're healthy! But the announcement... they said you were sick!
Sick of their cages. Sick of their lies.
Hello, little fan. I see you brought friends to bury my people.
Target identified. It's the traitor. Kill him!
We knew you would come. The Mother saw your malice.
You want to drop this mountain on our heads? You'll have to go through us first.
Strays! Hold the line! Buy me ten seconds to arm the payload!
Cyan! Make a choice! We fight the Wolf, or we fight the Captain! We can't do both!
I... I remember the town! I can't let him bury it!
That is an order, soldier! Defend the objective!

options.text: Follow Orders. We are Northern soldiers. We must stop Fenrir.
Stop Vance. Saving the town is more important than the mission.

steps.text: I... I can't let the invasion happen. Vance is right. If they breach the tunnel, Ironhold falls.
I'm sorry, Fenrir!
Cyan unleashed his rune magic, firing a bolt of energy at the Wolf.
You saw the cage, boy. And yet you still choose the handler.
Then die like a dog.
Cyan! NO!
The strike was too fast. Cyan didn't even feel it.
As he fell, the last thing he saw was Vance triggering the bomb.
The mountain collapsed. The town was buried. The Strays were buried with it.
In the end, you followed orders perfectly.
BAD ENDING: THE OBEDIENT SOLDIER
No! I won't let you murder innocent people!
Vance! Step away from the charges!
Traitors. I knew you didn't have the stomach for war.
If you won't hold the line, I'll detonate it now! We'll all go down together!
He is overloading the core! It will not seal the tunnel; it will shatter the ridge we are standing on!
Everyone! Get down!
Shields! Protect the tunnel entrance!
Rune of the Aegis!
The world turned white.
The explosion wasn't the calculated demolition Vance planned. It was a chaotic rupture triggered amidst a magical brawl.
The cliff edge crumbled. Vance screamed as he fell into the void.
The tunnel entrance collapsed, burying Fenrir's squad (and blocking the invasion route).
Cyan! Grab my hand!
Darkness took them.
Is... is everyone alive?
Barely. Vance is gone. Paste.
Look.
The town... it's still there. We stopped the main landslide.
Yeah. And we also just started a war.
Vance's 'Safety Inspection' just blew up a mountain. The South won't see this as a sealed tunnel. They'll see it as a failed first strike.
We didn't mean to...
Intent is irrelevant in geopolitics, Cyan. The first shot has been fired.
Cyan looked at the smoke rising from the pass. He had saved the town, but he had doomed the peace.
The Cold War was over.
Cyan woke up to the smell of antiseptic and old blood. His head pounded.
Vance... the bomb...
Relax, kid. We're alive. Somehow.
The tunnel is sealed. The Southern town was spared the worst of the landslide. We... succeeded. In a manner of speaking.
Awake. Good. The healers said you took quite a tumble.
Brandt! Captain Vance... he went crazy! He tried to bury the whole valley! We had to stop him!
Read the headline, Cyan.
What? But... that's a lie! Vance tried to kill everyone! Fenrir was defending his people!
History isn't written by what happened. It's written by what we say happened.
The official report is this: Captain Vance heroically detonated the charges manually after being ambushed by the traitor Fenrir. He gave his life to secure the border.
And 'The Strays'... you valiantly held the line against overwhelming odds to ensure his sacrifice wasn't in vain.
You're turning a war criminal into a martyr. And you're using us to sell it.
I am stabilizing the Kingdom. If the public knew a Northern Captain tried to massacre civilians, we would lose our foreign funding. We would lose the moral high ground.
But if Fenrir—the idol who betrayed them—is the villain? Then the people are united. They want justice. They want war.
I won't lie for you. I'll tell everyone what really happened.
Will you?
Because there is a second version of this report. One where 'The Strays' conspired with the traitor Fenrir to sabotage a vital military operation, resulting in the death of a decorated Captain.
The penalty for Treason in wartime is summary execution. For you. For Gabe. For everyone associated with your guild.
You son of a...
It is a simple choice, Eve. Be the Heroes who saved Ironhold... or be the Traitors who burn with Fenrir.
I need you alive. You are effective assets. Don't make me file the second report.
We... we held the line. Vance was a hero.
Excellent. Get some rest. The King is declaring a State of Emergency at noon.
You'll be receiving new orders soon. The North needs its heroes.
We are compromised. He owns us now.
Welcome to the real world, kid. No good deed goes unpunished.
Outside, the drums of war began to beat. Cyan listened, knowing that every beat was a lie he helped create.
The sun was setting over the Dragon's Tooth, painting the snow in shades of violet and bruised orange.
Cyan wasn't looking at the sunset. He was looking down into the valley, where the Southern town was disappearing into the twilight shadows.
You should be resting, Cyan. Your mana core was strained by that barrier spell.
I can't sleep. Every time I close my eyes, I see Vance falling. I hear Brandt's voice telling me to lie.
We're frauds, Lyrel. 'Heroes of the Border'. It's all garbage. We didn't save the border. We just... cleaned up our own mess.
Look down there. What do you see?
I see... shadows. The town.
Precisely. You see the town.
If you had not acted... if you had followed orders like a 'good soldier'... there would be nothing there but a scar on the mountain.
Thousands of lives are breathing tonight because you chose to be a traitor to a corrupt command.
Brandt can rewrite history. He can print whatever lies he wishes on that paper. But he cannot undo the reality of your action.
But Fenrir... he hates us now.
Perhaps. But his people are alive to hate us. That is a mercy.
You really think we did the right thing?
I do not think it. I know it.
When you cast that barrier... you did not use it to shield yourself. You used it to contain the blast. You risked your life for strangers who will never know your name.
That is not the act of a fraud, Cyan. That is the definition of a Warden. Of a protector.
I am... proud to stand beside you.
Thanks, Lyrel. I needed to hear that.
Alright, break it up, you two. If you get any more sentimental, I'm going to charge you extra for the tissues.
Wagon's waiting. Brandt cleared us for release. We're heading back to Porthumming.
We're going home?
For a few days, at least. Until the 'New Orders' come down.
Gabe's probably worried sick. Or he's sold the furniture to pay off the bookie. Either way, we should go.
Right. Home.
They're alive. That's enough for now.
They returned to Porthumming in silence.
They hoped for a break. A chance to heal.
But as they crossed the threshold of the guild, they didn't find peace. They found the inevitable.
And to think! They called them 'The Strays'! They called them misfits!
But who held the line at Ironhold? Who stopped the Traitor Fenrir from breaching the wall?
My team! The Saviors of the Border!
To the Strays!
We didn't stop Fenrir. We stopped our own Captain. We didn't save the wall. We blew up a mountain.
Gabe hops down from the table and wraps an arm around Cyan.
Look at him! Modest as a monk! That's a hero for you!
But modesty doesn't pay the tab. And it doesn't fit on a Guild Card.
Brandt sent the authorization this morning. High Command fast-tracked it.
Cyan. Step forward.
(Memory) Be the Heroes who saved Ironhold... or be the Traitors who burn with Fenrir.
No speeches necessary! Hand it over!
Congratulations, kid. You are officially a **B-Rank Adventurer** of the Northern Kingdom.
B-Rank... This was my dream.
And you earned it! The report said you used a massive barrier spell to contain the explosion when Vance detonated the charges. That's high-level defensive magic!
I used it to save...
To save the integrity of the mission. It was a necessary calculation.
Exactly! Smart AND strong! That's why you're B-Rank!
And the pay bump, Cyan! The commission on B-Rank quests is double. We're going to fill that vault back up in no time!
It's a lie. This rank... this skill... I got them because I agreed to lie.
It's not a lie, Cyan. You saved that town. You held that mountain back. That power was real.
The card? That's just the hush money.
Eve is correct. Your capability is genuine. How the world chooses to label it is a political fabrication, but your strength belongs to you.
I just... I thought being a B-Rank meant I was free. That I could choose my own path.
Nobody is free, kid. But at least now you're strong enough to survive the cage.
Strong enough to survive. That has to be enough for now.
Alright. They can't hear us down here.
Gabe? What's wrong? Is it the money again?
Forget the money. I need to know. And don't give me the 'Official Report' garbage you fed the press.
I watched every match Fenrir fought for three years. I saw him pull a strike because an opponent slipped. I saw him catch a goblin who fell off the catwalk.
Did he really do it? Did Fenrir butcher those engineers in cold blood?
No. He didn't.
The engineers... they were trying to do something terrible. Fenrir stopped them. He was protecting people.
I knew it. I knew that Wolf didn't have it in him.
Gabe, keep your voice down. If Brandt hears you talking like that, you're an accessory to treason.
The Kingdom has declared him a monster. You need to burn that pennant and forget his name.
No. I don't think I will.
And I'm not the only one, Eve.
What do you mean?
Since the announcement... I've had whispers. Regulars. Merchants. Kids who bought the wooden swords.
They're scared to say it out loud, but they don't buy it. You can't spend years telling people someone is a hero and then expect them to flip a switch just because the King says so.
There are underground betting pools starting up. Not for Fenrir to die... but for Fenrir to *win*.
People are asking: 'If the North lied about him retiring, what else are they lying about?'
If Fenrir comes back... if he leads an army here...
Half the North won't shoot at him. They'll cheer for him.
Exactly. High Command thinks they're fighting savages. They don't realize they're fighting an Icon.
If this war drags on... if the people get hungry and tired... and then Fenrir shows up offering a hand? The North won't just lose the war, Cyan.
It'll tear itself apart.
A civil war. Divided by loyalty to the Crown versus loyalty to the Idol.
I'm just saying... watch your backs. The enemy isn't just across the border. It's in the doubt.
Now, get out of here. Take the back exit. I have to go upstairs and pretend I believe the lies.
Go on! Get some rest, you B-Rank superstars!
He's right. Brandt is sitting on a powder keg.
And we're the ones holding the match.
The stage was set.
A Kingdom built on lies. A Hero built on guilt. A Villain built on love.
And a populace ready to burn it all down for the truth.
The morning sun rose over Aethelgard. The posters of Fenrir were being ripped down, replaced by notices of the 'Titan's Victory'.
Official Decree! The Southern Titan is declared Champion by Technical Knockout!
Fenrir has retired due to severe injury! All fighters have been moved to the Royal Sanctuary for quarantine!
He lost. He actually lost.
He was hurt, Gabe. He couldn't stand. The referee had to call it.
I know! But I thought... I thought the magic of the festival would save him! Or at least a comeback!
Come on. We have one last stop. Maybe... maybe the Bookie has a heart.
Look... I know the Titan was declared the winner. But then the lights went out! And everyone vanished! Surely that counts as a 'Voided Match'?
Nope. Ref waved his flag before the lights cut. Official ruling: TKO. Titan wins.
House keeps the pot. Thanks for playing, grandpa.
It's gone. The operating budget. The reward money. My retirement fund.
It's all gone.
Eve is going to be upset.
Upset? Cyan, 'upset' is when I forget to sweep the floor. This? This is a death sentence. I need to fake my own death. I'll live in the woods. I'll become a Druid.
We have to go back, Gabe. We can't leave Eve alone with the inventory.
The inventory... oh gods, the inventory...
The ride home was silent. Gabe stared at the floor, occasionally muttering 'stupid wolf' under his breath.
Cyan watched the trees pass by. He thought of Eclia. He thought of the empty arena. The North felt colder now. The gold paint had chipped away, revealing the rust underneath.
You're back early.
Honey, I'm hoooome! The... uh... the prodigal Guild Master returns!
I heard the news from a courier. Fenrir lost. TKO in the third round.
You... you heard?
I also checked the guild vault this morning. It's empty, Gabe. Even the emergency jar is gone.
I... I diversified our assets! Into a high-risk, high-reward venture! It just... happened to be the 'high risk' part that paid off!
So we have no money. None. We are actually poorer than when we started.
I brought you a souvenir! Look! A Fenrir bobblehead! It's a collector's item now that he's retired!
Eep.
Cyan.
Y-Yes, Eve?
Go to your room. Lock the door. Do not come out until you hear Gabe stop crying.
Understood.
I'm going to need a bigger spoon.
Mercy! I'm an old man! I have weak knees!
You gambled our rent money on a dog fight, Gabriel! Come here!
Run away! Tactical retreat!
Ow! My shin! Not the ladle!
I'm sorry! I'll never gamble again! I'll wash dishes for a year!
You'll wash dishes until you die!
And so, life in Porthumming returned to normal. The Strays were home. They were safe.
And thanks to Gabe, they were completely destitute.
But as Cyan sat in his room, listening to the chaos downstairs, he looked at his Fenrir pennant.
He realized that for the first time, he didn't want to be a hero like Fenrir. He just wanted to know where he went.
Phase 1: Complete.
Peace had returned to Porthumming. With the 'Silent Forest' investigation closed and the reward money distributed, the Strays found themselves with a rare commodity: free time.
You know, it's strange. Having money, I mean. I keep waiting for a monster to burst through the door or a mine to collapse.
Don't jinx it, kid. Enjoy the boredom. Boredom means nobody is trying to kill us.
It’s time! Pack your bags, lock the cellar, and pray to the gods of travel! It is officially the week of the Festival!
No.
Aw, come on, Eve! I haven't even asked yet!
It's the same week every year, Gabe. The leaves turn orange, the wind gets cold, and you get that stupid look in your eye. The answer is no. I'm not going.
The Festival? You mean the 'Festival of Fangs' in the Capital?
The one and only! The biggest tournament in the world! The best fighters, the best food, the best... everything!
And this year is special. Fenrir is going for his fourth consecutive title. Fourth! That's history in the making!
Fenrir... I've read about him. They say he fights with two scimitars and never draws blood unless he has to. A true honorable warrior.
Exactly! And we're going to see him live! I managed to snag two tickets for the full three-day pass. General Admission, but who cares? The atmosphere is better in the nosebleeds!
So... Eve. My favorite, most competent, most trustworthy former-colleague...
You want me to run the Guild while you're gone.
It's tradition! You know the regulars listen to you better than me anyway. And Old Man Hemlock is terrified of you. If you're here, no one will start a bar fight.
I hate that you're right.
Wait, Eve, you should come! It's a tournament! You love fighting. You even said you wanted to be a Werewolf once... Fenrir is a Wolf-kin! It would be amazing!
Kid, I spent ten years in the mud fighting for my life. To me, watching people bleed for applause isn't 'amazing.' It's a headache.
Besides, gladiatorial combat is just theater for cowards who like the sight of blood but are too scared to spill it themselves. I'll pass.
Oh. I didn't think of it like that.
What about you, Lyrel? You'd like the Capital! It's full of history and magic.
I must decline, Cyan. While I appreciate the invitation, the 'Festival of Fangs' represents a philosophy I cannot support.
To cage sapient beings—Beastkin or otherwise—and force them to combat for amusement is a violation of natural law.
I find no joy in such spectacles. I shall remain here. The guild library is in dire need of reorganization.
Buzzkills, both of you. It's not 'forced combat,' Lyrel. They're athletes! Superstars! They live better than kings!
But hey, more popcorn for us, right Cyan?
Yeah! I've never been to the Capital. This is going to be great!
Fine. Go. Have your boys' trip.
But Gabe? If the inventory count is off by even one copper when you get back, I'm selling your collection of rare tankards.
You wouldn't dare.
Try me.
We're leaving! Right now! Before she changes her mind about watching the bar!
Come on, rookie! Adventure awaits! And by adventure, I mean expensive meat-on-a-stick!
He is... very excited. For a man of his age.
Let him have it. It's the only time he smiles like that.
Besides... three days of quiet? No 'Strays' chaos? No ancient conspiracies? Sounds like a vacation to me.
Indeed. Peace and quiet. A rare treat.
They thought they were just going to watch a game.
They didn't know they were walking into the heart of the beast.
Aethelgard. The Crown Jewel of the North.
Cyan had read about it in books, but the reality was a physical blow to the senses. Massive white stone architecture draped in mile-long banners of crimson silk.
Magic wasn't just for fighting here; it was for decoration. Tiny, illusionary dragons danced above the streetlamps. The air smelled of roasted sugar and expensive spices.
It's... it's huge. There must be a million people here.
And every single one of them is here for the same reason we are, kid. The Festival!
Look at her. The Sunfire Arena. And we're going right to the heart of it.
Welcome, brave sirs! Welcome to the Sunfire District!
Get your official Festival gear here! We have Fenrir Claws! Minotaur Horns! And for the hungry adventurers, fresh Beast-Burgers!
Oh! You're... a Beastkin.
That I am, young master! A Lop-ear, born and raised in the Capital! Part of the proud Festival staff!
See? Eve was wrong. They aren't all treated badly. He has a job. He looks happy.
told you! The North is a melting pot, kid. We appreciate everyone who contributes.
Alright, my good hare! We need to look the part. Give us two Fenrir pennants and... four of those 'Wolf-Dogs'.
An excellent choice, sir! The Wolf-Dogs are made from the finest spiced pork. No actual wolves, I promise!
Keep the change! Buy yourself a carrot or something!
Thank you, sir! Blessings of the North upon you!
He seemed nice.
That's the beauty of the North, Cyan. We found a place for everyone. A hundred years ago, his ancestors would have been eating my crops. Now? He's a small business owner. That's progress.
Yeah. Progress. Peace through strength. Just like the stories.
FEN-RIR! FEN-RIR! FEN-RIR!
Hear that? That's the call! The Preliminary Match is starting! We're gonna miss the opening ceremony!
Wait up!
Cyan ran through the golden streets, surrounded by cheering families and laughing children.
For the first time since arriving in the North, he didn't feel like a refugee or an exile. He felt like he was part of something great.
He felt like he was home.
The roar was physical. Fifty thousand throats screaming in unison. The sound vibrated in Cyan's chest, drowning out his own thoughts.
Magical crystals suspended above the arena projected massive, illusionary images of the sand pit, ensuring even the cheap seats saw every drop of sweat.
Great seats, right?! You can smell the adrenaline from here!
It's loud! Is it always this loud?
Only for the best! Look! Here comes the Announcer!
Citizens of Aethelgard! Travelers! Patriots!
Welcome to the 100th Annual Festival of Fangs!
Today, we celebrate the strength of the North! We celebrate the taming of the wild! And to start us off... a clash of titans!
In the blue corner... weighing in at four hundred pounds of pure muscle... The crusher of stones... GORGE THE IRON-BACK!
He looks strong. Is he dangerous?
Gorge? He's a brawler. Hits like a truck, but he's slow. Watch his footwork.
And in the red corner... The Undefeated! The Pride of the Pack! The Three-Time Champion!
Give it up for... FEN-RIR!
FEN-RIR! FEN-RIR! FEN-RIR!
Wow. He really is a star.
Look at that confidence! That's a free man walking, Cyan. That's a king!
Fighters! Ready! BEGIN!
Gorge charged, swinging his massive fists. The ground shook with every step.
But Fenrir moved like water. He ducked under a haymaker, spinning gracefully to slash at Gorge's armor—not his skin. Sparks flew, dazzling the crowd.
He's fast! I can barely track him!
Gorge roared and slammed both fists into the sand. A shockwave rippled out. Fenrir leaped into the air, flipping over the Gorilla-kin's head.
Mid-air, Fenrir kicked off Gorge's back, landing perfectly on the other side.
Ha! The classic Fenrir Flip! He does it every year!
Gorge turned, panting. Fenrir didn't attack. He waited. He tapped his swords together, taunting his opponent. The crowd laughed.
Gorge charged again, blind with frustration. Fenrir stepped inside the guard, hooked Gorge's leg with his own, and swept him.
Gorge hit the sand with a thud that shook the stands. In a flash, Fenrir had a blade at the Gorilla's throat.
AND HE'S DOWN! FENRIR HAS THE KILL!
He... he spared him?
Gorge looked at the hand, then took it. Fenrir pulled the massive beast to his feet and raised Gorge's arm alongside his own.
MERCY! The Champion shows mercy! A victory for Fenrir! A victory for Honor!
See? Told you! Good clean fun! Nobody dies today!
That's sportsmanship, kid. That's how we do things in the North.
That was amazing! He could have killed him, but he chose not to. He's a true knight.
He's the best. Now come on, let's beat the rush to the souvenir stand. I need to get this pennant signed!
Cyan followed Gabe, his heart soaring. The fight had been thrilling, skillful, and bloodless.
He didn't notice that as Fenrir walked out of the arena tunnel, the smile instantly dropped from the Wolf-kin's face.
He didn't notice the guards waiting in the shadows with shock-batons, ready to escort the 'free man' back to his cage.
Did you see the footwork on the recovery? That wasn't just a dodge, Cyan, that was a 'Moon-Step Cancel'! He hasn't used that since the '98 Quarter-Finals against the Razor-Boar!
It was... fast. I think I missed the step part.

That's because you're watching the sword! Rookie mistake! With Fenrir, you have to watch the tail! The tail acts as a counterbalance for his center of gravity, allowing him to pivot at a sixty-degree angle without losing momentum!
I... see? So the tail is... the rudder?

Exactly! And Gorge fell for it hook, line, and sinker! The second Gorge committed to the haymaker, Fenrir had already calculated the torque needed to flip! It’s simple physics, really, combined with elite Wolf-kin agility stats!
Gabe had been talking for twenty minutes straight without inhaling. Cyan was trying his best to nod at the right times, but his brain was starting to melt.
And don't get me started on his stamina management! He didn't even pant until the third minute! That suggests he's been training at high altitude again. Probably the Dragon's Tooth peaks.
Wow, you really know a lot about him, Gabe.
Know him? I've studied him! I have his rookie card! I have a piece of the loincloth he wore during his first title match! Framed! Above my bed!
Uh... cool?
Alright. Discussion over. It's time to put our money where our mouth is.
Are we buying more souvenirs?
Better. We're investing.
Put it all on Fenrir. To win the Championship.
All of it, sir? The odds aren't great for the favorite. Returns are low.
I don't care about the odds! It's about loyalty! And when he wins, that low return is still free money! Put it all down!
Gabe! Wait! Is that... is that the guild's operating budget? And the reward money?
Every copper!
But... is that okay? What if he loses? What if he trips?
He won't lose. He's Fenrir.
But... Eve. Does Eve know?
Eve... doesn't need to know the details of our financial portfolio. We're diversifying, Cyan! It's smart business!
Besides, when we come back with double the gold, she won't be mad. She'll be impressed! She might even smile! A real smile, not the scary one!
I think she'll use the scary smile while holding a knife...
Details! Here, take your ticket.
They reached their hotel. It was nicer than the guild, with soft beds and a view of the illuminated arena.
Ah! What a day! The fights, the food, the impending financial victory... Life is good, kid.
It was fun. Really fun.
Do you really think he's treated well? The Gorilla, I mean. He looked... sad when he lost.
Sad? Nah, he was just disappointed. Like losing a card game. They'll give him a nice ice bath and a steak, and he'll be back in the prelims next year. Don't overthink it.
Get some sleep, Cyan. Tomorrow is Day 2. We've got the fan meet-and-greet in the morning. You might actually get to shake Fenrir's hand.
Trust me. It's only going to get better from here.
Only going to get better...
Cyan smiled, clutching his Fenrir pennant. He believed it. Why wouldn't he?
The North was a paradise. And he was finally part of it.
Look at that line! Half the city is here! But it's worth it. I'm gonna get him to sign my pennant!
It's going to take hours, Gabe. I'm going to walk up the side and try to get a look at him.
Don't get into trouble! And stay behind the velvet ropes!
Cyan found a vantage point between two banners. He expected to see the charismatic hero from yesterday, the one who had flipped over a gorilla and waved to the roaring crowd.

But up close, without the arena lights, the 'Gale of the North' looked diminished. His golden armor was polished, but the fur beneath it was matted with cold sweat. His eyes were glassy, staring at nothing.
A security guard stood directly behind the champion's chair. He didn't look like a coach. He stood like a statue, arms crossed, a heavy baton on his belt.
Fenrir rubbed his temple, his smile slipping for just a second as a visible wave of exhaustion hit him.
The guard didn't say a word. He simply cleared his throat—a sharp, dry sound—and tapped a gloved finger against the magical crystal bound to his own wrist.
The reaction was instant and visceral. Fenrir flinched as if he’d been burned. He immediately snapped his posture straight and plastered a wide, rigid smile back onto his face.
Thank you for coming. For the North.
Why did he jump like that? It was just a noise. He looks... he looks like a dog expecting to be kicked.
The line moved. Next up was a figure in a heavy, nondescript cloak.
The guard shifted his weight, his hand drifting toward the heavy baton at his belt. He glared at the hooded figure, a silent warning to move along quickly.
But the woman ignored him completely. She didn't present a paper for signing. Instead, she reached out and placed her hand gently over Fenrir's clenched fist.
Fenrir didn't look at the threatening guard. He looked solely at the woman. The glassiness vanished from his eyes, the fear dissolving in an instant.
He looked at her with an expression of pure, desperate adoration. It was the look of a drowning man seeing a lifeline.
The woman leaned in. Her lips barely moved.
The pain is mine, child. Tomorrow, the cage opens.
Fenrir mouthed a single word, no sound coming out, but the shape was unmistakable: 'Mother'.

The woman squeezed his hand once—a transfer of strength. Fenrir took a deep breath. For the first time all morning, his shoulders relaxed. He wasn't posturing for the camera; he was simply standing tall.
Line keeps moving. Let's go.
The woman didn't resist. She pulled back, turned, and disappeared into the crowd without looking back.
Mother? That woman wasn't a Wolf-kin. She was human.
But the way he looked at her... the fear was gone. Who is she?
I got it! I got the signature! He didn't look at me, and his hand was shaking a bit, but it counts!
Come on, let's get some lunch before the afternoon matches. I'm starving!
Gabe... did Fenrir look okay to you? He seemed... jumpy.
Jumpy? He's just pumped! That's the 'Eye of the Wolf', kid. Intense focus! Adrenaline!

Cyan looked back at the booth. Fenrir was smiling again, but the light in his eyes was gone now that the woman had left. The guard was whispering something in his ear, and Fenrir was staring blankly at the table.
Yeah. Adrenaline.
Cyan followed Gabe, but the doubts were taking root. The North's 'Hero' was terrified of his own guards, but looked at a stranger with love.
Cyan stood alone, trying to wash the noise of the crowd out of his ears with the silence of the night.
He didn't hear her approach. She moved like a shadow, her presence heavy but silent.
The Foxian Guard said there was a human boy who didn't cheer.
I had to see him for myself.
You... you're the woman from the autograph line.
And you are the boy who looked at the Champion and saw a prisoner.
Tell me, boy. What did you see in his eyes? Glory? Honor?
I saw... fear. He flinched when the guard tapped his wrist.
Good. You are not blind. But sight is useless without understanding.
The North says this is tradition. They say these beasts are violent by nature, and the Arena gives them purpose. That without the collar, they would kill us all.

options.text: It's cruel, but maybe it's necessary for peace.
It's wrong. No law justifies hurting someone like that.

steps.text: It looks cruel. I hate seeing them scared. But... Gabe says they used to burn villages. Maybe... maybe this is better than war? At least they're alive.
The woman let out a soft, disappointed sigh. It sounded like a mother watching a child make a mistake she couldn't stop.
Better than war? No. This *is* war. It is just a war where only one side is allowed to bleed.
You are a kind boy. But kindness without teeth is just another form of submission.
He is lost. The North has rooted itself too deep in his heart. I must burn the garden to save the flower.
It doesn't matter what they used to do. I saw Fenrir today. He wasn't a monster. He was a person in pain.
If peace means building a paradise on top of someone else's hell... then I don't want it.
You... haven't changed.
What?
Nothing. You possess a rare heart. One that feels pain that isn't your own.
He remembers. Even without knowing, he remembers. Perhaps... no. It is too late to stop. But perhaps there is hope for *him*.
Tomorrow is the Final. The Wolf fights the Titan.
Do not look away, boy. Watch closely when the leash snaps.
What is going to happen?
The inevitability of consequence.
Wait! Who are you? Why do you talk like... like you know me?
I am just a ghost from a story you forgot.
A ghost...
Cyan stood alone. He felt a heavy weight in his chest. Not fear, exactly. But a profound sense of loss.
Day 3. The Finals.
The air in the capital was heavy, electric with expectation. The playful energy of Day 1 was gone, replaced by a hungry intensity.
This is it, rookie! The big dance! The history books!
I couldn't sleep a wink last night. I ran the numbers in my head a thousand times.
Gabe... are you sure about this? Fenrir looked bad yesterday.
In the Semi-Finals... he didn't even dodge. He just took the hits so he could get close enough to break that Bear-kin's arm. He was limping when he left the ring.
That's just drama, Cyan! It's storytelling! The hero *has* to get beat up in the second act so the comeback in the third act feels earned!
Besides, Fenrir is a Wolf-kin. They heal fast. A good steak and a healing potion, and he'll be fresh as a daisy.
I heard them say they weren't feeding him. That he was in the 'Quiet Box'.
Psychological conditioning! It makes him hungry for the win! Trust the process, kid.
And the money? You put *everything* on him.
If he loses... we lose the guild funds. The reward from Brandt. Eve will actually kill you. She won't use a knife, she'll use a spoon because it hurts more.
She won't have to! Because he won't lose!
Look at the matchup! He's fighting 'The Titan'. It's some brainless lump of muscle imported from the South.
Speed beats power every time. Fenrir is going to run circles around that thing, tire it out, and then—BAM! The Fenrir Flip for the win!
A Southern monster?
Yeah. Rumor is it's one of those feral things from the jungle. Drugs pumping through its veins. A real monster, not a civilized fighter like our boy.
Civilized... Is that what we call a collar?
Hear that? That's the heartbeat of the North. Let's go get our seats. I want to be close enough to see the fear in that Titan's eyes.
They took their seats. But something was wrong. The crowd wasn't cheering Fenrir's name like Day 1. They were screaming for blood.
Bring out the meat! We want a show!
No more dancing! Kill or be killed!
Tough crowd today. They're just... eager. Yeah, just eager.
Citizens! The moment has arrived! The Defending Champion vs... The Challenger!
From the deepest jungles of the South... THE TITAN!
That thing... Gabe, look at its veins. It's glowing green.
That's the same sludge we saw in the Silver Mine! The toxic synthetic!
It's... uh... probably just a stimulant. Totally legal! Probably.
And... FEN-RIR!
He's not healed, Gabe. He's broken.
He's... he's saving his strength. Just wait. Just wait.
The bell rang. And for the first time, Cyan didn't want to watch.
He remembered the woman's words: 'Watch what happens when the leash snaps.'
The Titan roared—a sound like grinding metal—and charged. The ground shook with every step.
Move, Fenrir! Don't let him grab you!
Fenrir didn't try to block. He knew his bones wouldn't take the impact. Instead, he slid.
As the Titan's fist smashed into the sand where he had been standing a second ago, Fenrir pivoted on his good leg, spinning around the beast's flank.
He's fast! Even hurt, he's so fast!
Fenrir slashed his scimitar across the Titan's back. It was a perfect strike... but the blade just sparked against the creature's unnatural, gray hide.
His skin... it's like stone. The sword didn't even cut him.
It's fine! Death by a thousand cuts! Stick and move, Fenrir! Stick and move!
The Titan spun around with terrifying speed for its size, swinging a backhand blow. Fenrir ducked, weaving under the arm.
He saw an opening—the Titan's exposed throat. Fenrir coiled his legs to leap, to deliver a killing thrust.
But as he pushed off, his injured left leg buckled. The muscle, starved and beaten in the Quiet Box, simply gave out.
His leg!
The leap failed. Fenrir stumbled, falling forward into the sand instead of soaring through the air.
The Titan didn't miss the mistake.
The Titan's fist caught Fenrir mid-stumble. It wasn't a glancing blow. It was a collision.
Fenrir flew backward, tumbling across the arena like a ragdoll until he slammed into the stone barrier wall.
Get up! Shake it off!
Fenrir tried. He pushed himself up on trembling arms, coughing up blood. He raised his sword... but it was snapped in half.
Look at the Titan's veins! They're glowing green! The stimulants are kicking in!
The crowd, expecting a heroic comeback, grew impatient. The cheers died out, replaced by a low, ugly rumble.
Get up, you mutt!
Stop cowering! Fight back!
Boring! This is boring!
Why are they booing? He's being slaughtered!
Finish him! Kill him!
We paid for a fight, not a funeral!
HEY! SHUT UP! ALL OF YOU!
He's the Champion! He gave you three years of glory! He's hurt, dammit! Show some respect!
Sit down, old man! The toy is broken! Bring out a fresh one!
Gabe, look! The Titan!
IT'S ALL OVER! THE KING IS DEAD! LONG LIVE THE TITAN!
The crowd roared in anticipation of the splatter. The Northern 'civilization' leaned forward, desperate to see the life leave their hero's eyes.
NO!
The hammer blow fell.
But it never landed.
The magical lights shattered. The containment barriers hummed and died.
And from the darkness, a cold, thick fog began to roll.
Darkness. Absolute and heavy.
The crowd wasn't screaming in anger anymore. They were screaming in confusion. The magical amplifiers were dead.
Cyan? You okay? Stay in your seat! It's just a fuse!
I'm here!
This isn't a power outage. It's a shroud. I can't see anything...
But I don't need eyes to see.
Cyan pressed his thumb against his palm, tracing a simple, angular shape. A Southern technique for hunting in the pitch black.
Rivira.
The darkness vanished from his mind's eye, replaced by a monochrome map of life forces.
In the center of the ring, a massive bonfire of rage burned—the Titan. Its energy was jagged, chaotic, pulsating with the green taint of the drugs.
Beneath it, a smaller, flickering candle. Fenrir. His life force was dim, fading fast.
And then... a third light appeared. It didn't burn like the others. It was a void. A calm, deep well of energy moving between them.
Who is that?
Cyan watched the 'Void' step toward the 'Bonfire'. It reached out.
The Titan's rage didn't explode. It... drained away. The jagged lines smoothed out. The beast's soul went from a roaring fire to a calm ember.
She didn't strike it. She... quieted it. She drank the rage.
The Void moved to the Candle (Fenrir). It touched the flickering light.
Instantly, the candle flared brighter. A tether formed between them—a lifeline of pure mana.
The three lights moved together. Not fighting. Not struggling.
They moved in perfect sync towards the edge of the arena floor.
They're leaving. Together.
Suddenly, the lights dipped. They weren't walking out the gates. They were going *down*. Into the earth.
Tunnels. There are tunnels under the sand.
What... where did they go?
(Memory) Tomorrow is the Final. Watch closely.
(Memory) Not at the swords, but at the necks. Watch what happens when the leash snaps.
She knew. The woman on the balcony... she didn't just predict this.
She planned it.
Ladies and Gentlemen! Please remain calm! We have experienced a massive containment breach...
The safety protocols have automatically teleported all combatants to the secure medical facility below!
Oh, thank the gods. Safety protocols.
Teleportation! Of course.
Teleported? Wow. Must have been expensive to rig that up. Good thing they saved Fenrir, though!
It wasn't a teleport. And it wasn't a rescue.
The leash didn't break. She cut it.
What was that, kid? You look like you've seen a ghost.
Nothing. Just... glad they're safe.
The lie tasted like ash in his mouth. But he swallowed it anyway.
The Festival was over. The North had its spectacle.
But somewhere beneath their feet, the 'slaves' were marching south. And they weren't coming back as gladiators.
They were coming back as an army.
Are we there yet? My feet feel like they've been trampled by a grumpy direboar.
We've been walking for two hours. Your whining is more exhausting than the terrain.
It's not whining! It's a valid ergonomic observation! This path is terribly maintained. Not a single respectably placed root to step on.
It's a road, not your personal garden path, Tree-Hugger.
And you wouldn't know a good root if it tripped you into a puddle, Helmet Hair!
Alright, you two. The map says Oakhaven is just over this hill. We're looking for a 'weeping spirit'.
Probably a Grievewraith. Weak to silver and fire. We'll be in and out before second dinner.
Or it could be a lost soul tethered by sorrow! It might need kindness, not a pointy stick!
Everything with you is about kindness. You'd try to reason with a rockslide.
And you'd try to stab it! What's your point?
It was a familiar rhythm. Eve's cold pragmatism, Lyrel's bleeding-heart optimism. And me, somewhere in the middle.
It felt... normal. Like this could go on forever.
As dusk settled, we found a small clearing to make camp for the night.
Alright, we need firewood, something to eat, and the wards need to be set.

options.text: Ask Eve to forage for food.
Ask Lyrel to forage for food.

steps.text: Hmph. Fine. Better than trusting our dinner to someone who thinks moss is a spice.
A short while later, Eve returned.
In her hands was a bundle of pale, lumpy roots and some hardy-looking mushrooms.
Iron-head Roots and Stone Cap mushrooms. Tasteless, but packed with nutrients. They'll keep our stamina up.
Oh, lovely. We get to chew on delicious, nutritious rocks for dinner.
It's fuel, not a feast. Eat up.
Ooh, leave it to me! The forest always provides for those who listen!
Lyrel returned a little while later, humming a cheerful tune.
She carried a pouch overflowing with bright red berries and fragrant green herbs.
Sunberries! And a patch of wild King's Thyme! They'll make the stew taste divine!
(Sniffing a berry suspiciously) They're not poisonous, are they?
Of course not! The forest knows we're friends.
The forest doesn't have friends. It has a food chain. Let me see those.
As we ate, the familiar bickering softened into comfortable silence.
This reminds me of that time in the Northern pass, when we were pinned by that blizzard.
Oh, don't remind me! Eve's 'fuel' roots were frozen solid! It was like trying to eat a snowball!
They kept us from starving. Unlike your 'Sunberries', which would have been useless.
But we were so hungry, I tried to eat that spicy merchant's skewer I'd saved... big mistake.
Thinking back on it, even Eve cracked a small smile at the memory.
...You were an idiot.
Yeah. But we were warm.
The next day, we arrived in Oakhaven. It was a quiet, somber village, living in the shadow of a local legend.
A Phantasm. Not a Grievewraith. Weak to holy magic. My runes can-
Wait! Look at it. It's not angry. It's just... sad.
The spirit wept, its form flickering. It was pointing at a small, weathered toy horse on the ground.

options.text: Let Eve handle it. (Pragmatic Path)
Let Lyrel handle it. (Compassion Path)
Handle it yourself. (Empathy Path)

steps.text: Alright, Eve. Do it quickly.
My pleasure.
Eve's hands glowed with silver light. With a series of precise gestures, she cast a rune of banishment. The spirit shrieked, a sound of pain, not malice, and dissolved. The weeping stopped.
The chapel felt... empty. The job was done, but it didn't feel like a victory.
Lyrel, see if you can get through to it.
Of course.
Lyrel approached slowly, speaking in a soft, gentle voice. The spirit's weeping lessened, and it seemed to listen, but it couldn't respond. It was trapped in its loop of sorrow.
She had calmed it, but she couldn't free it.
Let me try. It's not a monster. It's a memory.
I didn't draw a weapon or a powerful rune. Instead, I focused on a simpler magic. A rune of connection.
I walked forward slowly and knelt, not looking at the spirit, but at the toy horse it was pointing to.
You lost your horse. You must have loved it very much.
The weeping hitched. A flicker of understanding. I reached out and gently picked up the toy.
It's okay now. I'll take care of it for you. You don't have to stay here and guard it anymore. You can go play.
A warmth spread through the chapel. The spirit of the child stopped weeping. It looked at me, and for the first time, it smiled. Then, it faded away like morning mist.
This was the path of The Strays. Not to fight the darkness, but to understand it.
Back in Oakhaven, we were rewarded with a hot meal and the softest beds we'd seen in months.
We sat around a table, drinking cheap ale that tasted like the finest wine.
To The Strays! Oakhaven's official ghost whisperers!
Don't get used to it. The next one will probably try to eat your soul.
And you'll be there to stab it before it can!
She raised her mug to Eve, who, after a moment's hesitation, clinked it with her own. A small, almost unnoticeable smile played on her lips.
Looking at them, at this small, dysfunctional, perfect family we'd built... I felt a profound sense of peace.
This was home. And I never wanted it to end.
Wow! Look at all the lanterns! And is that honey-cake? I think I can smell it from here! Can we get some, Cyan? Please?
It's a tactical nightmare. Too many civilians. Poor lighting. Multiple points of egress to monitor. Stay sharp.
Try to relax for one night, Eve. We earned it.
She just grunted in response, but I noticed her eyes weren't scanning for threats. They were lingering on a stall selling intricate silver jewelry.
He handed me a beautiful, unlit paper lantern. It felt heavier than it looked.
I looked at the lantern, then at Eve and Lyrel. My heart started beating a little faster. This felt... important.

options.text: Ask Lyrel. This seems like her kind of magic.
Ask Eve. She never gets to do fun stuff like this.

steps.text: Hey, Eve? D-do you want to... do this with me?
It's just, you're always so focused on the mission and wards and stuff. I thought... maybe you'd like to do something just... nice? For a change?
Me?
It's a silly superstition. Lyrel would appreciate the sentiment more.
Yeah, but... I want to do it with you.
The words just sort of fell out of my mouth. I felt my face get warm.
(Giggling) He's right, Eve! You can't spend the whole festival doing threat assessments!
Look at him, he's trying so hard to be charming! Go on before he short-circuits!
Lyrel's teasing was the perfect cover. It gave Eve an excuse, a way to accept without admitting she actually wanted to.
...Fine. But if we get ambushed by rogue honey-cakes, I'm blaming you.
Let's get this over with.
Great! I mean, okay. Let's go.
As we walked away, I glanced back at Lyrel.
I'll be right here... defending the honey-cakes from a hostile takeover!
She waved, her smile bright and wide. But for some reason, it didn't quite reach her eyes.
The path leading up the hill was quieter. Away from the noise, the silence between us suddenly felt... very loud.
So... uh... you do this a lot? Festivals?
No.
Right.
It's just... I've never seen so many food stalls. I saw one selling candied apples that were bigger than my fist!
They're mostly sugar. A poor nutritional choice. You'd get a sugar high, followed by a crash. Tactically unsound.
(Smiling) You can find a tactical flaw in everything, can't you?
She just grunted, but I saw the corner of her mouth twitch. It was her own weird way of caring.
I held the unlit lantern in my hands, looking down at the sea of lights from the festival below.
What do you think they're all wishing for?
An end to the war. A good harvest. For a sick relative to get better. Simple, predictable hopes.
Foolishness. You can't win a war or cure a plague by wishing on a candle.
Is it foolish to hope for things to be better?
Her smirk faded. She was looking at the lights, but I don't think she was seeing them.
Hope is a distraction. I knew a soldier once. A good man. He spent every night staring at a worn-out drawing his daughter made, wishing he'd get home to her.
He got so lost in his wish, so focused on the 'after'... he missed the glint of a scout's spyglass on the ridge. A single, tiny flicker of light.
He never saw his daughter again.
That's what hope gets you. It makes you blind to the moment. And the moment is all that matters.
The story was cold, and hard, and sad. It was the core of who she was. The world had taught her that looking forward gets you killed.
Back home, we had the first winter star. It was the only 'festival' we had.
Every year, the whole village would come out, shivering, and we'd all make a wish. We wished for food. For warmth. For the sickness to pass.
Simple, predictable hopes.
He looked at her, his expression earnest and open.
Most years, the wishes didn't come true. Winter was just as cold, and we were just as hungry.
But for that one night... nobody felt like they were cold and hungry alone.
Maybe hope isn't a distraction, Eve. Maybe... maybe it's just a way of sharing the burden.
She was silent. He hadn't argued with her logic. He had just shown her a truth his own life had taught him.
The cynical soldier had no counter for the hopeful survivor.
Right? So, if we all wish for this war to end, maybe the generals will feel it and just... decide to stop? It's worth a shot!
The sheer, undiluted naivety of the statement was so absurd, so... Cyan... that it broke the tension completely.
And she smiled.
It wasn't a smirk. It wasn't a grimace. It was a real, actual smile. Small, and gone in a second, but it was there. It lit up her whole face.
Hmph. You're a naive idiot.
She turned and started walking again, faster this time.
But this time, I knew I had seen something real. A flicker of light she thought she had hidden long ago.
And I smiled too.
We arrived at the top of the hill. The ancient oak tree was breathtaking, its branches heavy with the soft, warm light of a hundred wishes.
The air was still. It felt... sacred.
Wow...
It's... quiet.
Yeah.
We stood there for a moment, just breathing, side-by-side. The tension from the path was gone, replaced by a comfortable, shared silence.
I held up the unlit lantern. It felt like it was my turn to share my hope.
(Voice - quiet, but clear) I wish... I wish I'll be strong enough to protect the people I care about.
So that no one... so that *you*... never have to open that ledger again.
I looked at her as I said it. I wasn't trying to be charming or heroic. I was just making a promise.
And I saw it in her eyes. She understood.
(A little shy now) So... you got one? A wish?
...It's childish.
(A small, gentle smile) Come on. No one's listening but the tree. Is it for a new set of whetstones? An endless supply of tasteless, nutritious roots?
My stupid, gentle teasing was so out of place, so normal, that it completely broke through her composure.
A faint blush rose on her cheeks, beautiful in the warm lantern light. She turned her head away, but I saw the smile she was trying to hide.
(V.O. - Muttering, embarrassed but sincere) ...I wish for a quiet tavern... by the sea...
(V.O.) A place to just... stop running.
Her voice was so quiet, I almost missed it. A wish not for victory, but for peace.
We'll find it.
She looked back at me, the blush faded but a soft, unguarded warmth left in its place.
Together, we lit the lantern. Our fingers brushed, and this time, she didn't pull away.
We watched it float up, a single, silent prayer joining a constellation of hopes.
For what it's worth, rookie...
I hope you get your wish.
It wasn't a challenge. It wasn't a warning. It was a blessing.
We stood there for a long time, not speaking, just watching the lights. There was nothing left to say.
For the first time since leaving home, my dream didn't feel like a far-off story.
Looking at her, at the quiet strength I knew was always there... it felt real. It felt possible.
This was my journey. This was our beginning.
Oh, look, Cyan! They have woven star-blossoms! And is that roasted honey-nut cake? I *love* honey-nut cake! Can we get some? Can we? Can we?
It's a logistical chokepoint. If there were an attack, this area would be a deathtrap. Maintain situational awareness.
We'll maintain awareness all the way to the cake stall, Eve. Don't worry.
Eve just sighed. It was the long, suffering sigh of someone who had accepted their fate as the designated adult in charge of two hyperactive children.
He handed me the beautiful, unlit paper lantern.
I held the lantern, feeling its ceremonial weight. Before I could even think of what to do, I caught Lyrel's eye.
She gave me a quick, almost imperceptible wink. The signal. It was time for my grand performance.
Wow... a magical tradition. I wouldn't want to mess this up.
Hmm...
I made a show of looking back and forth between them, tapping my chin thoughtfully.
This seems to be about nature, and the earth... Lyrel, you know the most about this stuff. Would you mind... helping me out? So I don't accidentally wish for a plague of frogs or something?
(Sighing) Thank the spirits. I thought I was going to have to pretend to care about a tree's feelings.
You two kids have fun. Don't eat too much sugar, you'll be useless on watch tonight.
She was already turning away, her mind clearly on more 'sensible' things.
I'll be over by the smithy, where the sensible people are. Don't get lost.
And just like that, our brilliant, mastermind-level deception had worked. We had successfully tricked Eve into letting us go on a date.
(Whispering excitedly) Your acting is getting so much better! You almost sounded convincing!
(Whispering back) Hey, the 'Awkward Naive Boy' is a very complex role. It requires subtlety.
Uh-huh. Sure it does.
She dropped the formal act completely and laced her fingers through mine. Her hand was warm, and a thrill went up my arm.
(Her voice returning to its normal volume) Now come on, slowpoke! You promised me a honey-nut cake, and then we have a very important, super-secret wishing ritual to perform!
She pulled me along, weaving through the happy crowd. For a moment, we weren't soldiers or heroes. We were just a boy and a girl, sneaking away to be alone at a festival.
And it was perfect.
We found a quieter path that wound its way up the hill, away from the main festival grounds. Lyrel was practically bouncing, still high on the victory of our 'brilliant deception'.
I can't believe she fell for it. 'Secure the perimeter.' She's probably inspecting the structural integrity of the cake stall right now.
Hey, the safety of the honey-nut cake is a serious matter. And my acting was flawless, you have to admit.
Flawless? You almost tripped over your own feet when you asked me. I saw you.
That was part of the act! The 'Awkward Naive Boy' is a very complex role. It's all about... method acting.
(Giggling) Oh, really? Is that what you call it?
She suddenly stopped, pulling me into a small alcove, hidden from the main path by an old, mossy tree. The festival was just a soft glow and a distant murmur from here.

Before I could ask what was wrong, she let go of my hand, took a step forward, and playfully pinned me against the tree. Her face was inches from mine, a brilliant, mischievous grin lighting up her eyes.
(V.O. - A low, playful whisper) So, 'hero'... you saved my forest. You saved me from myself...
(V.O.) What are you going to do now that you've finally got the scary, berserker elf all to yourself?
Her teasing was confident, warm, and completely without fear. This was the Lyrel that existed only for me, the one who had faced her own darkness and come out stronger.
(V.O.) I don't know... I'm just happy to see you smile. A real, genuine smile. Not the one you wear for everyone else.
My words hit their mark. The mischievous grin on her face softened, the playful fire in her eyes giving way to a deep, profound warmth.
(V.O. - Her whisper now soft and vulnerable) ...I smile because you're here.
She rested her forehead against my chest. I could feel her breath, warm against my shirt.
(V.O.) Before you... before we healed the forest... I'd forgotten how. The smile was just... armor. To keep the ghosts out.
(V.O.) You don't need armor with me.
(V.O.) I know.
We stood there for a long moment, wrapped in a silence that was more intimate than any conversation. A silent acknowledgment of the battles we had already won together.
Come on. We have a wish to make.
She took my hand again. Her grip was softer this time, her earlier manic energy replaced by a quiet, certain joy.
Our joke of a date had just become something real.
We arrived at the top of the hill. The ancient oak tree was breathtaking, its branches heavy with the soft, warm light of a hundred wishes.
The air was still. It felt... sacred.
(Voice - a reverent whisper) Wow... You can feel the hope. It's like the tree has absorbed it all.
You were right. It's not about 'how it works,' it's about 'how it feels'.
I held up the unlit lantern, remembering the last time we'd talked about wishes.
So, what's the plan? A wish to heal all the sad places in the world?
No. That's our mission. That's what we do with our hands, together, every day.
A wish... a real wish... is supposed to be a little more selfish than that.
She took a step closer, her golden-green eyes, full of a love I was still getting used to, looking directly into mine.
I'm wishing for more nights like this.
After the wars are over, after the last scar on the forest has healed... I'm wishing for a quiet home, a warm fire, and you.
Her words were a direct hit to my heart. Simple, honest, and everything I'd ever wanted.
The hero from the stories could have the glory and the adventures. This was my dream.
That's not a wish, Lyrel.
That's a promise.
And in the warm, gentle light of the wishing tree, I leaned in and kissed her.
It wasn't a first kiss, full of nervous energy. It was the kiss of two people who had already faced the darkness together and had chosen each other.
It was a promise of a future we had already started building.
You're going to make me cry, you big idiot.
Happy tears only.
Always.
Together, we lit our lantern. We didn't say our wish aloud again. We didn't need to. It was the same one.
We watched it float up, a single, silent prayer joining a constellation of hopes.
She leaned her head on my shoulder, and I wrapped an arm around her. We stood there for a long time, not speaking, just watching the lights.
This was it. This was our beginning, and our happily ever after, all in one perfect, stolen moment.
The world had gone silent. The ringing in my ears faded, replaced by a profound, horrifying emptiness.
My mind was a blank slate, wiped clean by a grief too vast to comprehend. I just... knelt there. In the mud. In the silence.
How long I stayed like that, I don't know. Minutes? Hours? Time had lost its meaning.
My gaze fell to her side. Half-hidden in the mud, something caught the faint light of the rising sun.
The tarnished silver coin. Her lucky coin. The one she'd loaned me.
Slowly, reverently, my trembling fingers closed around it.
(V.O. - Muttering, embarrassed but sincere) ...I wish for a quiet tavern... by the sea...
(V.O.) A place to just... stop running.
A memory. So clear. So warm. A perfect, beautiful moment that felt more real than the cold nightmare I was living in.
And then it was gone. Leaving me alone in the cold. In the silence. Holding a worthless piece of metal.
A single, choked, guttural sob tore itself from my throat. It was the only sound I had made. It was the sound of my entire world breaking.
I clutched the coin in my fist, the sharp edges digging into my palm. The physical pain was a welcome distraction.
I looked at her peaceful, empty face. At the promise of a future that had been stolen from us. From me.
(Voice - a raw, desperate whisper) No...
This can't be it. It can't end like this.
It wasn't a shout. It wasn't a roar of anger. It was a denial of reality itself. A quiet, insane refusal to accept.
I would give anything...
I looked up at the grey, unforgiving sky.
(His whisper builds, cracking with absolute, soul-deep conviction) ...*anything*... to do it all again. To keep my promise.
And in the deepest, darkest corner of a broken boy's heart, something answered.
The dawn didn't rise. It shattered.
We found her in a ruined courtyard, a whirlwind of silver hair and dark energy. The White Phantom. Anne.
She was a force of nature. Lyrel's magic could barely slow her down. My runes sizzled and broke against her aura. Only Eve could match her, a desperate dance of daggers against a storm of steel.
But we weren't winning. We were losing. And Eve knew it.
With a brutal feint, she took a deep cut to her arm, luring Anne into an overextended strike.
The blast threw Anne back, creating a momentary opening. A clear, unguarded path away from the fight.
The path to survival.
(Shouting, clutching her wounded arm) The path is clear! Go, Cyan! That's an order! Keep your promise! SURVIVE!
Her words from the cave echoed in my mind. 'Promise me you will survive.' This was it. The moment she'd warned me about. The moment I was supposed to run.
I looked at the path to safety. Then I looked at her, standing alone against her ghost.
My promise was to be there for YOU! I'm not leaving you!
(VOICE, filled with fury and desperation) You damn fool!
I chose. I turned my back on her final wish, on logic, on survival.
I chose her.
The battle raged, now 2-on-1. We were desperate, clinging to a hope I had just created.
But Anne... she was a storm. And the storm was growing.
She raised her greatsword, and the air itself seemed to curdle. A sphere of raw, dark energy, crackling with crimson light, formed at its tip. It was aimed directly at me.
There was no time to dodge. No rune that could block it. This was the end.
Eve-!
She was already moving. She shoved me, hard, sending me tumbling to the ground.
And she took the full force of the blast.
I saw her armor crack. I saw her grunt, her teeth gritted in a mask of pure agony. She was thrown back, slamming against a ruined wall, but she got to her feet, panting.
She coughed, a single, sharp sound, turning her head away for a second. When she looked back, she was just... exhausted.
My defiant choice to stay, her impossible act of protecting me... something in that desperate, foolish loyalty broke through the static.
The crimson light in Anne's eyes flickered. For a single, impossible second, the storm stilled. A single tear traced a path down her cheek.
(VOICE, a distorted, pained whisper) ...E...ve...?
It was all the time she needed.
Eve saw it. The person she loved was back, and she was in agony.
And Eve, knowing she was living on borrowed seconds, made her final choice. Not to survive, but to save.
Rest now, Anne.
She lunged, not with the fury of a soldier, but with the grim mercy of a surgeon. Her daggers found their mark in the same instant that Anne's blade, in a final, confused spasm, ran her through.
It was over. We had won.
Eve! Eve, we did it! Are you okay?
She was slumped against the ruined wall... her armor was cracked and stained with blood. But she was alive.
(A weak, airy chuckle) Just... need to catch my breath, rookie.
Never... fight a ghost. It's... exhausting.
Relief washed over me so powerfully it almost brought me to my knees... We had won. And she was okay.
You were incredible. I... I thought I was dead. You saved me.
We saved each other.
We shared a look, a moment of profound, exhausted understanding.
She coughed, a dry, racking sound that shook her whole frame. She leaned her head back, her eyes closing for a moment.
Cyan... listen. Anne may be gone... but her army is still out there. They'll be disorganized... confused. But not for long.
She was right. The battle was over, but we were still deep in enemy territory.
What's the plan?
The path we came in... back through the ravine. It should be clear now that their commander is gone. But we need to be sure.
Go. Scout ahead. Make sure there are no patrols regrouping for a counter-attack. Find us a safe path out of here.
It was a logical order. The smart thing to do. The only thing to do.
What about you? I can't leave you here alone and wounded.
(Her eyes still closed, the faint smile still on her lips) I'm a Shadow, remember? Hiding is what I do best. I'll find a place to rest... and wait for your signal.
I'll be right behind you. Just... find us a way home, rookie.
Find us a way home. The words echoed the wish from the festival. The tavern by the sea.
Okay. Okay, I'll be quick. I'll find the safest, fastest way out.
Don't move. And don't fall asleep, you hear me?
No promises, rookie.
I gave her one last look, my heart swelling with a mixture of pride, relief, and a fierce determination to get her home safely.
Then, trusting her, I turned and ran to scout the ravine, leaving Eve to her well-deserved rest.
(V.O., sharp and urgent) Cyan! You have to get to that ridge and stop that voice! NOW!
Eve's voice was a cold spike of logic in a hurricane of chaos. The 'Good End' path. The winning move.
The path to the south ridge was clear, a corridor of relative calm carved out by Lyrel's desperate struggle.
